The Opus Cirro Is a Lightweight, Self-Inflating Camper With a King Bed
24 photos
Photo: Opus Camper
Life is all about compromises, choices, and priorities, though not necessarily in that order. The Opus Cirro hybrid camper would like to take some compromises out of the equation, while making the choice easier for future RV-ers.
Opus Cirro is the latest offering from UK-based Opus Camper , a company that maintains a strong presence on the international stage, including partners in Europe, the U.S., and Australia. It's also the smallest and lightest offer from that catalog, which in itself is notable, seeing how they specialize in lightweight and compact solutions.
Opus Camper does hybrid campers – towables that travel tiny and then expand into home-like habitats at camp with the help of canvas extensions. What makes these hybrid trailers different from other hybrids from the same niche is the fact that Opus uses a patented Air System to have them self-inflate. It's all fun and no work for you once you've opened their clamshell-like base, is what this means.
All this trickles down to the Opus Cirro, the newest member of the self-inflating camper family. First teased at the 2026 Dusseldorf Caravan Salon and then at the 2026 NEC Caravan in Birmingham the following month, the Cirro is ready for its big, formal debut.
Photo: Opus Camper The new model isn't yet available, but the pre-order books are finally open. Last time we looked at it, buzz online claimed that Opus was eyeing an early 2027 delivery date, which seems to be confirmed in the video tour at the bottom of the page. It will be just in time for the new summer camping season.
The Cirro targets a very specific type of customer, which will go a long way to explain why it's so basic in terms of equipment. It's designed for the occasional camper who drives either an electric vehicle (EV) or a compact car, and who maybe is upgrading from a traditional tent.
It's a basic, stripped-down version of the bigger models Opus offers, but in return, it offers to that camper the possibility to bring along two more family members or even as many as six if they add extra kit, to choose their own gear in terms of cooking and bathroom facilities, and a high degree of garageability.
Photo: Opus Camper This hybrid camper might not offer much in terms of actual comfort beyond the perk of sleeping off the ground, under a nice shelter, but it does have several pros – a light weight and compact form factor being among them.
On the road, the Cirro is a hair over 3.5 meters (11.4 feet) long from tip of the drawbar to the rear and just 1.8 meters (5.9 feet) wide. It rides on a single-axle chassis that can be ordered braked or unbraked, and presents – in road mode – as a shell of insulated aluminum panels. Opus themselves describe it as "super-cute and dinky," which is true. It's also perfect for a standard garage and will tow with ease.
Empty weight is just 500 kg (1,102 lbs), while maximum permissible weight is 750 kg (1,653 lbs). You can add a pair of optional racks on the lid of the clamshell to carry up to 75 kg (165 lbs) of cargo there, whether kayaks or storage boxes.
Photo: Opus Camper At camp, you open the lid of the trailer and plop it on sturdy support legs. That area will become the suspended base of the bedroom, which comes with tent liners, an LED sleeve, opening windows with screen mesh, and most importantly, a bed that's bigger than a standard king.
The upper section is tent canvas, though not the one Opus uses for their bigger models. This one is technical cotton fabric that promises to be waterproof, durable, and breathable, and it inflates by means of two pumps powered by twin 3000mAh OPUS Blow Bank batteries built directly into the air tube structure. The batteries are removable for charging and the entire system is protected from the elements.
Bigger Opus campers boast installation as fast as a couple of minutes. The Cirro takes a bit more, even though it's smaller, because the Air System itself is stripped down. Opus says complete setup at camp takes "under 10 minutes," which is still decent if you consider it's zero effort on your part.
Photo: Opus Camper With the structure in place, you get a camper that's 4.6 meters (15 feet) long and 2 meters (6.5 feet) high inside, with a sense of space you probably won't find in similar products. The Cirro comes with several large windows throughout and two skylights, one more LED sleeve in the living space, and a seating area comprised of a longer bench that extends into a single bed and a small bench.
Tucked in a dedicated storage compartment at the front is a removable, foldable table that will fit inside on rainy days. Open cubbies for storage are included under the longer bench, as are USB-A and USB-C outlets. At camp, the Cirro hooks up to the mains with a 230V connection.
Opus says that the Cirro can be optioned with a Comfort Package that adds custom graphite alloy wheels, a large 180-liter (6.3 cu-ft) metal storage box on the tongue, a 35-liter (1.2 cu-ft) compressor fridge, a spare tire with carrier mounted underneath, sideskirts, a windbreak kit, and upgraded upholstery in a suede-like fabric.
Photo: Opus Camper They also highlight compatibility with the older Air Sun canopy or the full awning kit, which adds more living space that you can use either for fitting more beds (up to four) or a kitchen. These will also add to the final price, but pre-ordering a bundle will supposedly save you a lot of cash.
Since we're on the topic, the base Cirro is priced at around around £13,500, which would be approximately €16,100 or $17,900 at the current exchange rate. The Cirro Comfort Package is obviously more expensive, at around £15,000 (€18,000/$19,800).
